AND '@task Title @assign @Name @due 2026-05-20 @priority high'. critical_code_review_comments: parse_task_command in ai_service.py is regex-based and works correctly for the documented syntax, but: (1) the title regex stops at @assign|@due|@priority — any OTHER @ token in the title will be silently dropped. Low risk but worth a doc note. (2) _parse_due returns None for unrecognized strings (e.g., 'next Monday', 'May 15'); task is still created with due_date=null — acceptable graceful degradation.

_handle_inline_task uses asyncio.create_task fire-and-forget — exceptions are swallowed silently. Consider adding a logger.exception inside a try/except so future failures are visible in /var/log/supervisor/backend.err.log.
Assignee prefix-match has a subtle gotcha: if two members share a prefix (e.g., 'Priya' and 'Priyansh'), the first encountered in db.users iteration order wins. Currently no collision in demo data.
server.py is now 1171 lines — splitting into routers remains advisable (carried forward from iteration 4).
